_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟡 Minor_

**Add a blank line after the new heading.**

Line 6 is immediately followed by text, which violates MD022.

<details>
<summary>🧹 Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-## 2025-06-18 - Unused Validation Schema
-**Vulnerability:** The product API contained a comprehensive Zod validation schema (`productSchema`) in `sanitize-core.ts` but the actual route handlers (`POST` and `PUT`) manually extracted fields without using this schema, leading to a Stored XSS vulnerability in the `description` field.
+## 2025-06-18 - Unused Validation Schema
+
+**Vulnerability:** The product API contained a comprehensive Zod validation schema (`productSchema`) in `sanitize-core.ts` but the actual route handlers (`POST` and `PUT`) manually extracted fields without using this schema, leading to a Stored XSS vulnerability in the `description` field.
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
## 2025-06-18 - Unused Validation Schema

**Vulnerability:** The product API contained a comprehensive Zod validation schema (`productSchema`) in `sanitize-core.ts` but the actual route handlers (`POST` and `PUT`) manually extracted fields without using this schema, leading to a Stored XSS vulnerability in the `description` field.
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🧰 Tools</summary>

<details>
<summary>🪛 markdownlint-cli2 (0.20.0)</summary>

[warning] 6-6: Headings should be surrounded by blank lines
Expected: 1; Actual: 0; Below

(MD022, blanks-around-headings)

</details>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In @.jules/sentinel.md around lines 6 - 7, The new heading "2025-06-18 - Unused
Validation Schema" in .jules/sentinel.md is missing a blank line after it
(violates MD022); insert a single blank line immediately after the heading line
so the heading is separated from the following paragraph/text, ensuring the file
follows Markdown linting rules.
```

</details>

_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Guard optional fields to avoid wiping data on partial updates.**

Lines 212-215 coerce missing fields to `''` and write them into `updates`, so a PUT that omits name/description/category can clear stored values and generate empty slug/sku/meta. Only sanitize when provided and conditionally include those fields.

<details>
<summary>🛠️ Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-const sanitizedName = sanitizeText(body.name);
-const sanitizedDescription = sanitizeHtml(body.description || '');
-const sanitizedBrand = body.brand ? sanitizeText(body.brand) : undefined;
-const sanitizedCategory = sanitizeText(body.category);
+const sanitizedName =
+  body.name !== undefined ? sanitizeText(body.name) : undefined;
+const sanitizedDescription =
+  body.description !== undefined ? sanitizeHtml(body.description) : undefined;
+const sanitizedBrand =
+  body.brand !== undefined ? sanitizeText(body.brand) : undefined;
+const sanitizedCategory =
+  body.category !== undefined ? sanitizeText(body.category) : undefined;
@@
-const slug =
-  body.slug ||
-  generateProductSlug(
-    sanitizedName,
-    body.condition,
-    sanitizedConditionDetail
-  );
+const slug =
+  body.slug ??
+  (sanitizedName
+    ? generateProductSlug(
+        sanitizedName,
+        body.condition,
+        sanitizedConditionDetail
+      )
+    : undefined);
 const sku =
-  body.sku ||
-  (body.name
-    ? generateSlug(sanitizedName).toUpperCase().substring(0, 20)
-    : undefined);
+  body.sku ??
+  (sanitizedName
+    ? generateSlug(sanitizedName).toUpperCase().substring(0, 20)
+    : undefined);
 
-const meta_description =
-  body.meta_description || generateMetaDescription(sanitizedDescription);
-const meta_title = body.meta_title || sanitizedName;
+const meta_description =
+  body.meta_description ??
+  (sanitizedDescription
+    ? generateMetaDescription(sanitizedDescription)
+    : undefined);
+const meta_title = body.meta_title ?? sanitizedName;
@@
-const updates = {
-  name: sanitizedName,
-  description: sanitizedDescription,
+const updates = {
+  ...(sanitizedName !== undefined && { name: sanitizedName }),
+  ...(sanitizedDescription !== undefined && {
+    description: sanitizedDescription,
+  }),
@@
-  sku: sku,
-  slug: slug,
+  ...(sku !== undefined && { sku }),
+  ...(slug !== undefined && { slug }),
@@
-  condition_detail: sanitizedConditionDetail,
+  ...(sanitizedConditionDetail !== undefined && {
+    condition_detail: sanitizedConditionDetail,
+  }),
@@
-  brand: sanitizedBrand,
+  ...(sanitizedBrand !== undefined && { brand: sanitizedBrand }),
@@
-  category: sanitizedCategory,
+  ...(sanitizedCategory !== undefined && { category: sanitizedCategory }),
```
</details>


Also applies to: 274-320

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@apps/web/src/app/api/products/`[id]/route.ts around lines 210 - 236, The
current sanitization block unconditionally reads and transforms fields (e.g.,
sanitizedName, sanitizedDescription, sanitizedCategory,
sanitizedConditionDetail) from body and later writes them into updates, which
will overwrite existing DB values on partial PUTs; change the logic to only
sanitize and add fields to the updates object when the corresponding body
property is present (use presence checks like if ('name' in body) / if
(body.name != null) for name, description, brand, category, condition_detail,
slug, sku, meta_description, meta_title). For slug/sku/meta fallbacks
(generateProductSlug, generateSlug, generateMetaDescription) only run and assign
them when the dependent input is provided or when you intend to overwrite;
otherwise omit those keys from the updates so partial updates do not clear
stored values.
```

</details>

**Add global cleanup for the fetch mock.**

Line 80 sets `global.fetch` at module scope without restoration, which leaks into other tests. Use `vi.stubGlobal()` and restore with `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` in an `afterAll` block.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
+import { afterAll, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';
 
 // Mock fetch for embedding generation
-global.fetch = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
+const fetchMock = vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
   ok: true,
   json: () => Promise.resolve({}),
 });
+vi.stubGlobal('fetch', fetchMock);
+
+afterAll(() => {
+  vi.unstubAllGlobals();
+});
```
</details>

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
In `@apps/web/src/app/api/products/xss.test.ts` at line 2, The test sets
global.fetch at module scope and never restores it, leaking into other tests;
replace that module-scope assignment by using vi.stubGlobal('fetch', ...) to
install the mock and add an afterAll block that calls vi.unstubAllGlobals() to
restore globals; update the test file's setup so beforeEach still resets state
as needed and the new afterAll cleans up the stubbed fetch (reference
vi.stubGlobal, vi.unstubAllGlobals, and afterAll in xss.test.ts).
```

</details>
